about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Shontel M. Brown

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONGRESSIONAL BLACK CAUCUS HIT THE GROUND RUNNING IN AUGUST
statements.title: CONGRESSIONAL BLACK CAUCUS HIT THE GROUND RUNNING IN AUGUST
sentences: Trump and his family, with their tax cuts, stock trades, and new military contracts got rich, while working-class people got the bill.

Now, they are just one illness away from financial ruin, all because the Trump administration and Republican majorities in Congress have enacted the largest cuts to Medicaid in history, along with letting the Affordable Care Act tax credits expire.
Remember last year, the other side of the aisle raised, rushed, and sprinted--sprinted to pass tax cuts for the rich.
It is time to cancel the cuts and the illegal wars, stop the corruption, kill the kickbacks and the insider trading, and give the American people their country back.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HAITI TEMPORARY PROTECTED STATUS
statements.title: HAITI TEMPORARY PROTECTED STATUS
sentences: Last week, the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to terminate the Temporary Protected Status, also known as TPS, for hundreds of thousands of Haitians, not because Haiti is safe, not because the facts have changed, but because this administration wants more people for ICE to deport.

That law ripped healthcare away from millions of Americans, cut food assistance for families and children, made it harder to afford college--all to hand out massive tax breaks to the wealthiest people in America.
Meanwhile, the wealthiest 0.1 percent received tax cuts worth nearly a quarter million dollars just last year.
I call it a big, ugly law, because there is nothing beautiful about taking healthcare and food away from families to pay for tax cuts for billionaires.
One year later, the verdict is in: Working families paid the price, and the wealthiest Americans cashed the check. ____________________
I will ask the simple question: How has Trump's big, ugly law helped the American people?

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ANOTHER BLIGHT ON AMERICAN HISTORY
statements.title: ANOTHER BLIGHT ON AMERICAN HISTORY
sentences: This conservative Supreme Court has taken a wrecking ball to the Voting Rights Act, one of the greatest achievements of the civil rights movement.
Finally, Mr. Speaker, we must confront the center of this crisis: an unacceptable Supreme Court.
We will organize, mobilize, and use our voices.
We will fight this in Congress.
We don't have a voting rights majority in this body right now, but we soon will, and we will restore the Voting Rights Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FARM, FOOD, AND NATIONAL SECURITY ACT OF 2026
statements.title: FARM, FOOD, AND NATIONAL SECURITY ACT OF 2026
sentences: Input costs keep rising, driven by reckless tariffs and the reckless war in Iran.

Farmers are being squeezed from every direction, and this bill offers them next to nothing: no farm aid; no solution to rein in fertilizer or diesel prices; no protections against USDA reorganizations or funding freezes; no attempt to end the tariffs destroying export markets or restore the trade relationships farmers depend on; and false promises again and again on year-round E15.
Working families aren't doing any better.
Republicans used the big, ugly law to slash $187 billion from SNAP and handed that money straight to the wealthiest Americans.
The NRCS currently includes composting facilities as a conservation practice standard, but assistance under this standard is limited to the construction of a structure to facilitate composting.
This amendment proposes specifically to designate composting as a practice standard that is not tied to a structure but simply on activities to produce composts from organic waste.
The amendment also requires review of a current composting facility practice standard and has provisions to address greenhouse gas emissions.
This could also reduce food waste, and I support the amendment.
Mr. Chair, this partisan bill is not it, and I urge my colleagues to oppose it.
Mr. Chair, I rise in opposition to this amendment.
Mr. Chair, as I expressed in my earlier remarks, I continue to oppose this amendment, and I urge all Members to oppose this amendment.
Mr. Chair, wildfires are a significant threat to rural communities, and I support efforts to bring down the cost of forest treatments that would help protect these communities.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: 2027 PRESIDENTIAL BUDGET REQUEST WILL MAKE LIFE HARDER
statements.title: 2027 PRESIDENTIAL BUDGET REQUEST WILL MAKE LIFE HARDER
sentences: Not the billionaires who just got tax cuts, not Elon, not the Trump family, not White House insiders cashing in on trades ahead of market-moving announcements, no.
Trump's war machine will be paid for by working people, just like his tax cuts for billionaires were paid for by working people.

In the last year, Trump has made the largest cuts to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act in history and the largest cut to food assistance in history, all to make the richest Americans richer and the biggest corporations bigger.
Mr. Speaker, I don't know who is winning Trump's war with Iran, but I can tell you who is losing the war: Everyday people in America.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FREE AND FAIR ELECTIONS
statements.title: FREE AND FAIR ELECTIONS
sentences: He keeps talking about taking over elections, and his number one legislative priority is the SAVE Act.
The SAVE Act requires documents that millions of citizens do not have in order to vote.
Even the new REAL ID drivers' licenses we all had to get don't meet the standard.
The SAVE Act also ends online and by-mail voter registration.
If Congress passes the SAVE Act, it will be the first time since Jim Crow that our legislature has acted to make our democracy smaller, not larger.
In 2003, it was tax cuts for the wealthy and a war we were told would be quick and necessary.
Did you know demand for private jets is booming after President Trump gave tax cuts to the wealthiest Americans last year?
Now, the President wants $200 billion more to fund an unauthorized and unacceptable war in Iran, a war that is already jacking up costs from the gas pump to the grocery store.
We were told there is no money for healthcare, so Republicans gutted Medicaid and refused to extend Affordable Care Act tax credits.
There are billions for billionaires.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ICE COMING TO SPRINGFIELD, OHIO
statements.title: ICE COMING TO SPRINGFIELD, OHIO
sentences: Legal status today, illegal status tomorrow.
He said: ``If I have to create stories . . . that is what I am going to do.'' Well, those stories dehumanized Haitians who were here legally working and rebuilding a city.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HISTORY IS WATCHING
statements.title: HISTORY IS WATCHING
sentences: When agents show up in unmarked vehicles wearing masks without warrants, without body cams, targeting people based on their race or the sound of their voice, and detaining people without cause, that is not law enforcement.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: STRENGTHENING AGENCY MANAGEMENT AND OVERSIGHT OF SOFTWARE ASSETS ACT
statements.title: STRENGTHENING AGENCY MANAGEMENT AND OVERSIGHT OF SOFTWARE ASSETS ACT
sentences: This is legislation that will improve the acquisition process for Federal agencies, help the government better manage software needs, and ultimately save taxpayer dollars.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 5457, the Strengthening Agency Management and Oversight of Software Assets Act.
I will also take a moment to recognize the late Congressman Connolly, who worked tirelessly on this legislation and who had introduced the SAMOSA Act prior to his passing.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to support this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WORKING PEOPLE PAY THE PRICE
statements.title: WORKING PEOPLE PAY THE PRICE
sentences: He is working for us if we are wealthy, well-connected, and don't want the Epstein files to see the light of day.
No, he is driving up our costs by imposing reckless tariffs and cutting SNAP, Medicaid, and ACA subsidies.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: STORIES FROM HOME: THE HUMAN COST OF EXPIRING HEALTHCARE TAX CREDITS
statements.title: STORIES FROM HOME: THE HUMAN COST OF EXPIRING HEALTHCARE TAX CREDITS
sentences: We can't afford the largest cuts to Medicaid and to the Affordable Care Act in this Nation's history.
In fact, some of the Whitest and most rural parts of America rely on the Affordable Care Act the most, including a lot of farmers in my State of Ohio.
Mr. Speaker, 38,000 people in my district are facing huge healthcare cost increases because of Trump's ACA cuts.
I thank Talia for sharing her story, and I want to assure her we will not give up on this fight.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NORTHEAST OHIOANS ARE GETTING SQUEEZED
statements.title: NORTHEAST OHIOANS ARE GETTING SQUEEZED
sentences: Madam Speaker, I have just come back from our district work period in northeast Ohio, and let me tell you, Madam Speaker, there is nothing better than being home being in our churches, in our union halls, and our community centers listening to the people I serve.
I heard how tariffs are jacking up prices, crushing small businesses, and threatening workers.

I heard how the President's cancellation of community safety funding will make our neighborhoods less safe, and I heard how his attacks on unions at the VA and FEMA will ripple right into the private sector, hurting working men and women everywhere.
So Donald Trump can enrich himself and his billionaire allies while everyday, hardworking Americans pay the bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: They will cut benefits, cut eligibility, or cut public safety, education, housing, and mental health programs just to stay afloat.
Don't reward the rich on the backs of hungry Americans.
Mr. Speaker, I ask unanimous consent to amend the rule to make in order the amendment at the desk that protects against any cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong opposition to this rule and the underlying bill.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to reject this provision, reject this rule, and reject this betrayal.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: Let's be clear, Republicans are paying for massive tax cuts for millionaires and billionaires by cutting $300 billion from SNAP.
That is not fiscal responsibility.
What they call skin in the game is unworkable.
The hits to States' budgets would be massive, up to $4.5 billion over 10 years in Louisiana, $4 billion in Alabama, $15 billion in Florida, and $7.5 billion in my home State of Ohio.
This plan will take away food from kids, working families, veterans, seniors, and the disabled.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong opposition to this rule and the underlying bill.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to vote ``no.'' Protect SNAP.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS WOMEN AND FAMILIES
statements.title: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS WOMEN AND FAMILIES
sentences: Today, I rise to share the story of Cheryl from Cleveland Heights, a constituent whose life could be upended by cuts to SNAP and Medicaid.
None of them can work, and they depend on SNAP and Medicaid to survive.
Mr. Speaker, I am proud to stand with Leader Jeffries and my Democratic Women's Caucus colleagues to oppose harmful cuts to food and health assistance.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION: ERASING BLACK HISTORY
statements.title: DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION: ERASING BLACK HISTORY
sentences: President Trump and his administration have attacked diversity, equity, and inclusion programs in the government, in schools, and in the private sector.
If something goes wrong somewhere, anywhere, in their mind, diversity, equity, and inclusion is to blame.

In President Trump's vision, every Black American on the job, every woman, and every immigrant is a DEI hire, a DEI hire who is blocking more qualified White men from the jobs and the positions of power that are rightfully theirs.
Last month, in my district, a man checked out 100 books on Black, Jewish, and LGBTQ topics from the Beachwood Public Library.

It is part of a disturbing wave we are seeing across the country, a wave fueled-- sometimes with a wink and a nod, sometimes with a bullhorn--by leaders who should know better than to fan the flames of division for political gain, a wave normalized by the Secretary of Defense banning books about diversity and deleting Pentagon websites highlighting the service of women, LGBTQ people, and minority servicemembers, including Major League Baseball legend Jackie Robinson.
Mr. Speaker, what happened in my district isn't just censorship.
In America, for every $100 in wealth owned by White households, Black households own $15.

In 1890, Ohio Representative John Patterson Green, the first Black-elected official in Cleveland, authored legislation to establish Labor Day as a State holiday 4 years before it became a Federal holiday.
If we don't reckon with our past, we will never understand the present, and we will never build a better future.
That is why we are going to keep fighting back.

Mr. Speaker, as my colleagues and I have highlighted over this past hour how this administration is intentionally attacking Black history, which is an attack on American history, we will not allow this attack to continue.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRUMP'S FIRST 100 DAYS
statements.title: TRUMP'S FIRST 100 DAYS
sentences: They have tried to fire Federal workers without cause, detain and deport people without due process, freeze and deny congressionally appropriated funds, and seize sensitive taxpayer information through the Treasury and Social Security.

The disastrous policies of this White House are hurting the entire country, absent a few of his billionaire buddies, of course, but it is the people that many of us represent that are the most at risk.

This is a White House that constantly diminishes and dismisses Black achievement; a White House that blames anything and everything on diversity, equity, and inclusion; a White House that is trying to defund our public safety programs and our police; a White House that is trying to defund our schools, and a White House that has rolled back Federal antidiscrimination policies that have been on the books since 1965--that is right--since 1965.
We are talking about healthcare and taking away Medicaid coverage.

We are talking about nutrition and taking away SNAP benefits from families and so much more, because the budget they voted for called for $880 billion in cuts to Medicaid and $230 billion in cuts to SNAP.
I represent 280,000 people on Medicaid, 160,000 people on SNAP.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FIRST 100 DAYS
statements.title: FIRST 100 DAYS
sentences: He has enacted tariff chaos, driving up the cost of fertilizer, fuel, and equipment.
He has launched a trade war, again putting farmers at risk of retaliatory tariffs that will dry up export markets.
Working families in urban, suburban, and rural communities across America are footing the bill for Trump's chaos.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
statements.title: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
sentences: President Trump and unelected billionaire Elon Musk are waging an all-out assault on Federal workers.
In just 2 weeks, they have engaged in unlawful union busting, budget freezes, and civil servant layoffs all designed to intimidate, weaken, and dismantle our Federal workforce.
In northeast Ohio, Federal workers process Social Security checks for seniors.
This is part of a coordinated effort to erode trust in government because the President and his billionaire buddies want it to fail.
Most notably, it is to hand billionaires and their corporations massive tax breaks while sticking it to working Americans.
Or is it a government of the billionaires, by the billionaires, and for the billionaires?
Federal workers don't serve a President or his billionaire buddy.
Let me say that again: Federal workers don't serve a President or his billionaire buddy.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of more than 9,000 Federal workers in my district and their dedicated colleagues across the country.
They serve the American people, and we stand with them.
